subtitle: "A practical walkthrough for turning a messy project list into a structured plan using Google's AI assistant."

> **In short:** Open Gemini in your browser or app, pick a model, and use one ongoing chat to brainstorm tasks, build a timeline, and draft the messages you need — copying the bits you want as you go.

When a big project is looming, the hardest part is usually just starting. Gemini, Google's AI assistant, can act as a thinking partner that helps you move from a messy pile of ideas to a checklist you can actually follow.

**What you need first**
- A Google account (free — any Gmail address works)
- A modern browser, or the Gemini app on iPhone or Android (both free)
- About 15 minutes for your first run-through
- A rough idea of what you're planning — even one sentence is enough

## Step 1 — Open Gemini and start a fresh chat

Go to **gemini.google.com** in your browser, or open the Gemini app on your phone. Sign in with your Google account if prompted. Once you're in, look for the **"New chat"** button — usually a plus icon or a "New chat" label near the top-left of the screen. Tap it to open a clean conversation.

After tapping, you'll see a blank message thread with an empty text box at the bottom and a fresh greeting from Gemini above it. There should be no earlier messages visible.

You'll know it worked when the screen shows an empty thread with the input box at the bottom and no previous conversation history above it.

💬 *Example prompt to type next:* "Help me plan a 50-person community charity lunch in October with a $500 budget."

## Step 2 — Pick the right model for planning

Before sending your first message, look for the **model selector** — usually a dropdown menu at the top of the chat, or sitting near the send button. Common options include **"Gemini 2.5 Flash"** (faster, good for everyday planning) and **"Gemini 2.5 Pro"** (slower but stronger at complex reasoning). For most planning tasks, Flash is plenty.

After selecting, you'll see the chosen model name displayed in the selector. Your next message will be answered by that model.

You'll know it worked when the dropdown clearly shows the model name you picked (for example, "Gemini 2.5 Flash").

💬 *Example setting:* Model selector → "Gemini 2.5 Flash"

## Step 3 — Brainstorm with a clear prompt

Click the text box at the bottom of the chat and type a prompt that covers the basics: what you're organizing, who's involved, your budget, and the deadline. The more context you give, the better the answer. Press **Enter** or tap the **send** icon (a paper-airplane-style button) to submit.

Within a few seconds, Gemini will reply with a structured list — usually numbered or bulleted — breaking your project into prioritized steps like booking a venue, drafting a guest list, or estimating catering.

You'll know it worked when you see a numbered or bulleted list of concrete actions, not a generic "here are some tips" paragraph.

💬 *Example prompt:* "I'm organizing a 50-person community charity lunch in October. Budget is $500 AUD. List the first five things I need to lock in, in priority order."

## Step 4 — Build a timeline in the same chat

Stay in the same chat — don't start a new one. Type a follow-up asking Gemini to map the steps onto a calendar. Because you're still in the same conversation, it already has the full context of your project.

After a moment, you'll see a week-by-week breakdown, often in table form or as a clear list of weeks with tasks under each. If one week looks overloaded, just ask in plain English to redistribute the work.

You'll know it worked when you see dates or week numbers attached to specific tasks, and you can say "move week 3 to be lighter" without re-explaining the project.

💬 *Example prompt:* "Turn those five steps into a week-by-week timeline starting eight weeks before the event. I work full-time, so keep weekdays lighter."

## Step 5 — Draft your messages to collaborators

Still in the same chat, ask Gemini to write the emails, social posts, or volunteer invites you need. Be specific about tone and audience.

You'll receive a ready-to-edit draft, formatted with a subject line, greeting, and body. You can then copy it — look for a **"Copy"** icon near the response, or highlight the text and copy as usual — and paste it into your email or notes app.

You'll know it worked when you can highlight the draft text cleanly and paste it into Gmail or your messaging app without having to reformat anything.

💬 *Example prompt:* "Write a friendly but polite email to local bakeries asking if they would donate bread rolls for our charity lunch. Keep it under 150 words."

## Common mistakes

- **Starting a new chat for every follow-up.** Each new chat loses the previous context. Stay in the same conversation so Gemini remembers your project details.
- **Sending vague prompts like "help me plan an event".** Add the date, headcount, budget, and tone. The more specific you are, the less editing you'll need later.
- **Copying the AI's first answer without checking.** AI drafts are a starting point — always read them, swap in real names, and double-check any numbers or claims before sending.
- **Picking the wrong model by accident.** If an answer feels weak or generic, check the model selector — a stronger model (like Gemini 2.5 Pro) often helps for trickier planning tasks.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: Use Gemini to plan a house move, a holiday itinerary, or a weekly meal plan with a shopping list — the same brainstorming → timeline → draft pattern works for any multi-step project.
- **At work**: Map out product launches, structure team workshops, or generate meeting agendas and follow-up emails. Keep each project in its own chat so the context stays tidy.
- **If you're just getting started**: Open Gemini today and ask it to plan one small thing, like a weekend garage clean-out. You'll learn the rhythm in one session.
